caption:
Nvidia has lost about $1.7 trillion in market value since early October, CNBC reports — six straight weekly drops, its longest losing streak since 2012. Its CEO of 33 years resigned Thursday.

The part getting less attention: Axios reports the Commerce Secretary was sent a classified warning about the CEO's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy BEFORE his department cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's advanced chips. He has now agreed to testify to the Senate, and Huang has agreed to a closed-door session in the House.

My take: the affair is the headline, but the money story is who was warned, when, and what got approved anyway.

If you hold an S&P 500 fund, Nvidia is in it. Earnings land Tuesday. Should chip-export approvals get an independent review? 👇
